sources.note: No mention of Karkin/Carquin (the vocabulary was only identified as Karkin by Beeler 1961); Costanoan 'Phonetics' section (pp. 249-251) covers vowels/consonants of the other mission dialects and says nothing about accent or stress.

sources.citation: California Language Archive (Survey of California and Other Indian Languages). Language page 'Karkin'. https://cla.berkeley.edu/languages/karkin.html
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Karkin is attested only in a single, short vocabulary recorded by Father Felipe Arroyo de la Cuesta in 1821.' Further reading = Beeler 1961, Callaghan 1988, Okrand 1989 (all flagged 'PDF - may not be publicly available'), Hinton 2001, Milliken/Shoup/Ortiz 2009. Nothing on phonology or stress; the CLA collections list for Karkin (langid=585, saved) returned no archival items.

Sole documentation is the 1821 Arroyo de la Cuesta vocabulary from Mission Dolores; extinct by the 1850s; no phonology section; reference list = Beeler 1961 (doi:10.1086/464632), Callaghan 1988 (doi:10.1086/466096), Callaghan 1997 (doi:10.1086/466313), Golla 2007, Milliken 1995, 2008.
